title: Audit: crypto2dev 2026-04-20
notes:
Confidence: FIPS gate provider-callback coverage: 100% (all 40+ callbacks in all 10 wolfssl provider files verified, all gated correctly). Framework-level gate for one-shot ops (DO_SIGN/VERIFY/AGREE): NOT verified — filed as WOLFKM-w4c.1. Key material leak risk: 5% — all zeroization paths traced; memzero_explicit used throughout; ECDH Z zeroed before return; RSA digestinfo zeroed; ioctl op structs zeroed on all exit paths. UAPI stability risk: LOW — no implicit struct padding holes found; reserved fields mostly validated; raw wolfCrypt errno leak to userspace is the active defect. Sections with zero findings: FIPS provider callback gates (S1), crypto misuse (S2), kernel driver discipline (S3), FIPS operational risks (S6), efficiency (S7). What would raise confidence: (1) lockdep run to verify no sleeping-under-lock paths introduced by future patches; (2) wolfCrypt call trace coverage tool to enumerate every wc_*() callsite and verify each has the correct check convention; (3) CMVP lab review of ioctl_do_{sign,verify,agree} dispatch paths for framework gate gap (WOLFKM-w4c.1).
Confidence update (pass 3 — direct code read): FIPS gate framework coverage: 100% — all 21 callback dispatch points in crypto2dev_fd.c verified by direct read, gates present including DO_SIGN/VERIFY/AGREE (WOLFKM-w4c.1 was false positive, now closed). Key material leak risk: <1% — every key-bearing path traced to a memzero_explicit call: ioctl op structs (all 4 containing key bytes hit out_zeroize/out_zero on every exit including copy_from_user failure), all 11 provider sess_free/key_free implementations call memzero_explicit(ctx) before kfree, inbuf_clear uses memzero_explicit, ECDH Z zeroed before every exit from agree(), RSA digestinfo and verify expected[] zeroed on all paths, outbuf memzero_explicit'd at fd_release and before key_export_private read. Residual <1%: (a) wc_AesFree/wc_ecc_free internal zeroization is not verified — if wolfCrypt's Free functions leave key schedules in memory inside the struct, memzero_explicit(ctx) after Free still covers it since the struct is embedded, not heap-allocated by wolfCrypt. (b) Kernel page reuse (slab allocator) outside this code. These are system-level, not code-level, risks. What would eliminate residual: wolfCrypt source review of wc_AesFree/wc_FreeRsaKey/wc_ecc_free to confirm they zero internal state, or CMVP lab test. No code changes needed from this analysis.
